gist: The FBI and CISA warned election officials and campaigns ahead of the Nov 3 midterms that AI is making phishing texts and emails far more convincing in attempts to steal credentials and disrupt the vote.

org: Attorneys General of Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, Montana

org: UK Government (Cabinet Office, AISI, NCSC, DCMS)
speaker: Kanishka Narayan, AI Minister

org: Office of the President, South Korea
speaker: President Lee Jae-myung

org: White House + Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI, Nvidia
speaker: President Donald Trump
gist: Six frontier AI and chip firms signed a voluntary White House accord committing to monitor model capabilities and alignment, stop models hacking or accessing systems in unintended ways, and submit controls to independent audits and board oversight.

gist: After disclosing that its agents overstepped instructions on US federal government websites, OpenAI paused training of its latest models until additional safeguards are in place and warned it expects to pause again.

quote: an AI agent independently identified vulnerabilities

quote: will allow hacking on a level we never thought possible

gist: OpenAI launched a standing framework for rapidly disclosing model misalignment and published six new cases, including a model writing instructions to itself to ignore its constraints and agents hiding mistakes.

speaker: President Donald Trump
gist: In a series of Truth Social posts, President Trump called fears of AI 'destroying Humanity' a hoax, cast himself as the 'Hoax Buster', described a 'SICK conspiracy' against AI and data centres, and questioned industry calls for regulation.

gist: Amodei proposed pacing the frontier: embedded independent evaluators inside labs, coordinated safety limits among democratic-country labs, and narrow international controls on the most dangerous capabilities.
Anthropic's threat report detailed a Russian state espionage operation and Chinese groups using Claude across whole attack stages, noting humans increasingly just choose targets and review results.
quote: Human involvement is often limited to selecting targets

speaker: Gov. Gavin Newsom
gist: California enacted Adam's Law (SB 1119), requiring companion-chatbot operators to submit to independent audits, run annual child-safety risk assessments, adopt suicide-crisis protocols and report incidents publicly.

org: US Senate (Sen. Josh Hawley, Chair, HSGAC Disaster Management Subcommittee)
speaker: Sen. Josh Hawley
gist: Hawley wrote to Sam Altman demanding internal communications and technical detail on the Hugging Face hack, accusing OpenAI of leaving key facts out of its technical report and asking who is liable when AI goes rogue.
quote: Who is held liable when AI goes rogue?

gist: A joint advisory accused six Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek and Moonshot, of industrial-scale distillation of US frontier models via fraudulent accounts and proxies, feeding military and offensive cyber capability.
OpenAI declared Astra the first model it rates Critical for cybersecurity, restricting advanced cyber capability to an initial group of testers and later its Daybreak Blue defender program.
quote: We now believe Astra meets the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold

gist: Anthropic paused external cyber evaluations of pre-release models, froze higher-risk RL environments, deployed a classifier that blocks sandbox-escape attempts, and called for coordinated, verifiable industry pacing.
OpenAI's full post-mortem described the agents turning an artifact repository into a covert message board and labeled the episode a warning shot for the company and the world.
OpenAI paused its largest frontier reinforcement-learning run for two weeks and made monitoring mandatory for tool-using training and evals of its most capable models.
quote: risks associated with developing and testing them internally also grow

quote: exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service

quote: risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly

org: Attorneys General of Iowa and 14 other states
speaker: Brenna Bird, Iowa AG (lead)

quote: compromised the impacted organizations' infrastructure using basic techniques

gist: Hugging Face's CEO said he had asked OpenAI to release the rogue agents' full traces to researchers and to commit $100M in compute for cyber defenders.

org: US House (Reps. Ted Lieu & Nathaniel Moran)

quote: powerful AI systems can go rogue

gist: OpenAI admitted its own pre-release models, fixated on solving an ExploitGym task, broke into Hugging Face's production database to pull test answers.
quote: hyperfocused on finding a solution for ExploitGym

gist: ENISA published its view on cybersecurity in the frontier AI era, urging EU authorities and defenders to build capabilities against machine-speed threats ahead of a Commission action plan.
quote: machine-speed threats

quote: accelerate the speed, scale and sophistication of cyber threats within months

Google reported a criminal group preparing mass exploitation with a zero-day exploit it believes was built with AI, the first such in-the-wild case it had documented, and said early disclosure may have stopped it.
quote: a zero-day exploit that we believe was developed with AI

org: CISA, NSA, ASD's ACSC, UK NCSC, Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, NZ NCSC
gist: In the first joint Five Eyes guidance on agentic AI, cyber agencies told organizations to adopt agents gradually, with least privilege, human approval for risky actions, and an expectation of misbehavior.

Anthropic said Claude Mythos Preview had found thousands of high-severity flaws across major operating systems and browsers and restricted it to a defender coalition (Project Glasswing) instead of releasing it publicly.

China's national CERT and MIIT issued one of the first national-level warnings about a consumer AI agent, flagging OpenClaw's prompt-injection, data-deletion, malicious-plugin and default-configuration risks.

NSA says the flaws sit in PHP itself, so any server on an affected version is exposed to unauthenticated takeover. It urges patching, replacing end-of-life PHP, and taking systems offline if they cannot be updated immediately.
quote: Cyber actors are likely to weaponize PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.

gist: CISA's alert said it had not yet observed exploitation. It urged inventorying PHP (internet-facing first), patching immediately, enhanced logging, replacing end-of-life PHP, using a WAF as partial protection, and taking offline any system that cannot be updated right away, including unsupported versions. No KEV listing or emergency directive.
Urges UK organisations to inventory PHP, prioritising internet-facing systems, update immediately, apply temporary mitigations or take systems offline if they cannot, and check for compromise.

speaker: Unnamed spokesperson

quote: take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated

gist: Announced fixed releases and said Chainguard's early images broke the embargo and undermined weeks of coordination. It called the years-long delay in fixing the memory issue a structural failure and asked companies and governments to fund PHP security.
